spans.s: bhikṣā (IE 8-4), a grant or endowment; cf. ekādaśa-Rudra-bhikṣā (EI 32), an endowment in the gods’ name.
Bhikṣu (EI 7, 21; CII 3; ML), Buddhist monk, also called Śākya-bhikṣu.
Bhikṣu-hala (LL), ‘the monks’ land’; rent-free land in the possession of Buddhist monks.
Bhikṣuhala-parihāra, cf. Prakrit Bhikhuhala-parihāra (HRS), known from Śātavāhana records as a number of privileges relating to rent-free land belonging to the community of Buddhist monks.
Bhikṣuṇī (EI 25; CII 3; LL), feminine form of Bhikṣu; ‘a Buddhist nun’; also called Śākya-bhikṣuṇī.
Bhikṣuṇī-saṅgha, cf. bhikkhuṇī-saṃgha (EI 23), a community of nuns.
Bhikṣurāja (LL), title of a pious [Jain] king.
Bhikṣu-saṅgha (EI 26; CII 4), community of Buddhist monks.
